races.name: Download The At The Races App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Front-runner with recent poor form but lightly weighted, needs to bounce back from disappointing Lingfield effort
runners_data.comment: Ran poorly at Lingfield on Tuesday and Sisterandbrother looks his yard's best chance
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run and he beat only one in 11.5f Lingfield handicap ten days ago; not ruled out though if back on his A-game.

runners_data.name: Green Team
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good nick, three wins this year and solid recent Southwell fourth gives confidence
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time winner (including over C&D) in 2025 for Ian Williams; in good nick for his present yard too, fourth of eight in 1m3f Southwell handicap eight days ago; not out of things.

runners_data.name: Arth's Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent Southwell win, Richard Hannon yard in form and James Hills jockey booking catches eye
runners_data.spotlight: Finally opened his account at Southwell in April and he followed it with a solid third of eight there eight days ago; ought to be thereabouts again.

runners_data.name: Relocal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won for Varian in January, showed promise for new yard with Yarmouth third
runners_data.spotlight: Scored at Chelmsford (1m5f) for Roger Varian in January; not disgraced for his new yard with third of six in 1m6f Yarmouth handicap nine days ago, so he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Lenny's Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner and course winner returning from disappointing turf effort, better on AW surface
runners_data.comment: Promising stable debut in March (1m2f, AW); return to turf a plus; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on the AW at Lingfield this year until a below-par sixth on turf in 1m2f Windsor handicap 18 days ago; this course winner can bounce back here.

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing first-time cheekpieces again after good Windsor second, trip increase suits
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in November; got back on track in first-time cheekpieces when second of 13 in 1m2f Windsor handicap 18 days ago; can go well again back up in trip with the headgear retained.

runners_data.name: Jack Sparowe
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing blinkers after impressive Yarmouth win, 6lb rise but momentum strong
runners_data.comment: On a losing run but well treated and the change of headgear could give him a lift
runners_data.spotlight: Blinkered when ending a lengthy losing sequence in good style at Yarmouth nine days ago, drawing clear last 1f; up 6lb but another bold showing is on the cards with headgear retained and good amateur Henry Callan up.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won this race in 2024, two wins from last three including Beverley victory two days ago
runners_data.comment: Won at Doncaster this month and ran well at Southwell six days ago; now 2lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Has made a bright start for his current yard and made it two wins from his last three runs in 1m4f handicap at Beverley two days ago; also took this in 2024, so he's a player under a 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Now Then Wendy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from hurdles after 27 days, question marks over fitness and form
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 1m4f AW winner for Hughie Morrison in 2023; seemed only poor over hurdles for Steph Cameron subsequently, pulled up at Uttoxeter 27 days ago; returns to this sphere for her new handler with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Someone's Wish
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from jumping after 36 days, former course winner but fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Course scorer (for Robert Eddery) in 2023; a fair winning hurdler/chaser for Gordon Elliott since but pulled up over hurdles at Perth last month on final run for yard; more needed for his new stable.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing blinkers for new yard, shaped well at Beverley despite 36-day absence
runners_data.spotlight: Remains winless but he shaped well in first-time blinkers for his new yard when second of eight in 8.5f handicap at Beverley last month; can go well again in retained headgear if his stamina holds out over this much longer trip.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong AW form including two course wins, disappointed on turf return but back on preferred surface
runners_data.spotlight: In fine form on the AW in 2026, scoring twice over C&D in April; beat one back on turf at Bath last time but no surprise to see him get back on track here.

races.paceDynamic: Pleasant Man and Green Team are the only confirmed front-runners, likely to set an uncontested, sustainable pace over this 1m4f trip on the all-weather. With 10 of 12 runners adopting hold-up tactics, this creates a massive pack of closers waiting to pounce in the straight. The lack of early pace pressure means the leaders can dictate fractions and potentially kick clear when the field fans out. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with proven tactical speed who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Pleasant Man and Green Team maintain a steady gallop and kick clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows them to conserve energy before unleashing their finish, while the Hold-up brigade gets strung out too far back. Form horses with tactical pace prove superior to one-dimensional closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair goes too slow and gets swamped by the wall of closers in the final 2f
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get perfect positioning as the pace quickens late, with in-form runners like Sisterandbrother and recent winner Jack Sparowe finding gaps. Quality prevails over tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Pleasant Man and Green Team engage in a pace duel that compromises both leaders
scenarios.body: The early tempo becomes unsustainable, setting up perfectly for mid-division runners like Arth's Gold who can track the pace without getting involved. Smart positioning by jockeys becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the AW specialists get the fractions wrong and an outsider strikes with perfect timing
scenarios.body: Form horses disappoint as an improving type like Glitter Code or returning jumps horse finds the gaps at the right moment. Class tells less than race-reading ability.

watchPoints.text: Sisterandbrother ran just two days ago at Beverley - watch for signs of a quick turnaround affecting his usual finishing kick
Pleasant Man and Green Team both adopt prominent styles - monitor if they engage too early and compromise each other's chances
Jack Sparowe wears blinkers again after his impressive Yarmouth win - watch if the headgear continues to sharpen his finishing effort
Now Then Wendy and Someone's Wish return from jumping after long breaks - observe their early positioning for fitness clues
Several hold-up horses including Arth's Gold and I'd Go Maniac rely on gaps appearing in the straight - watch the traffic situation

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Always Happy
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with superior class ratings but needs to handle the return to turf after all-weather success
runners_data.spotlight: Siyouni filly who got off to a winning start in 1m Southwell novice in March; beaten at odds-on but advanced her form when second of 12 under a penalty in 1m Lingfield novice 17 days ago; she holds very good form claims.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 217-day break with Oisin Murphy taking the ride for trainer with modest recent form
runners_data.spotlight: 13-2, promising neck second of six in maiden at Doncaster (7f, soft) on her debut in October; winner has gone in again since, so this Lope De Vega filly must enter calculations with Oisin Murphy in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Hatour
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who showed promise last time and benefits from Gosden's strong recent record
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation filly; has shaped with promise on both her runs, running on well late on when third of nine in 7f Lingfield novice on her return 17 days ago; this step up in trip promises to suit; player.

runners_data.name: Flagpole
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 184-day absence but looked encouraging on debut for powerful stable
runners_data.spotlight: 15-2, encouraging debut fourth of 14 in 1m Southwell novice in November; this Starspangledbanner filly seems sure to build on it after a break.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sky
runners_data.note: Improved last time in prominent position and represents trainer with excellent recent strike rate
runners_data.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly who took a big step forward from her debut when a running-on third of six in 7f Yarmouth novice 29 days ago; she's open to further progress, especially over this longer distance.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Surf
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse still learning her trade but quickest turnaround of the field at just 11 days
runners_data.spotlight: Oasis Dream filly; still looked green but improved when sixth of ten in 1m Windsor maiden 11 days ago; can do better still, especially once handicapping.

races.paceDynamic: Always Happy will dictate terms from the front with only Hollywell Stream and Venetian Sky likely to race prominently early. This creates a sustainable tempo rather than a searching gallop, with the majority of the field (Hatour, Flagpole, Moonlit Surf) positioned in mid-pack or held up. The modest early pace will allow hold-up horses to stay in touch before the real racing begins in the final three furlongs. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can finish, particularly those able to quicken from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Always Happy maintains an uncontested lead into the straight
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop allows closers to get into contention before unleashing their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Hatour and Flagpole benefit most from the tactical setup, with their late-running styles perfectly suited to pick off a lone leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Hollywell Stream or Venetian Sky challenge Always Happy early
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates a more searching test that suits horses with proven stamina. Always Happy's front-running style thrives under pressure while Hollywell Stream benefits from the stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages
scenarios.body: A messy, slowly-run affair turns into a sprint where positioning and luck become crucial factors. Horses with natural speed like Venetian Sky and Moonlit Surf can capitalise on the tactical nature, while class tells in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Always Happy kicks clear turning for home without challenge
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds an unassailable advantage that the closers cannot reel in despite their finishing efforts. Her superior class rating and front-running style prove decisive when given an easy time of it.

watchPoints.text: Always Happy's adaptation back to turf after two all-weather runs could prove crucial to her front-running tactics
Hollywell Stream's fitness after 217 days off despite looking promising on debut at Doncaster
Hatour's ability to get a clear run from her hold-up position with Robert Havlin needing to time his challenge perfectly
Flagpole's sharpness returning from a winter break for the Gosden team who excel with returning horses
The pace development in the first half-mile will determine whether this becomes a sprint or stamina test

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anad
runners_data.spotlight: 150,000euros yearling; fourth foal; State Of Rest half-sister to winners Miami Matrix (7f/7.5f including AW; RPR 90), Ob La Di (10.3f/12.3f; 89) and Baltic Fleet (1m1f 2yo; 88); dam French Listed-placed 1m2f/1m3f winner (95); powerful stable is 2-4 with 2yos on AW this year; interesting.

runners_data.name: Rosevannion
runners_data.spotlight: 82,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Zoustar half-sister to winners Saariselka (6f 2yo; RPR 89), Israaj (1m/1m1f including 2yo/dirt/KSA; 84) and Kohoof (Spanish 6f-1m); dam unraced half-sister to two sprint winners; trainer 18% with AW 2yos (five seasons); market check suggested.

runners_data.name: Zarakova
runners_data.spotlight: 190,000gns yearling by Zarak; first foal; dam Group-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 99), half-sister to Canadian 1m Grade 2 winner Elizabeth Way, out of 1m Group 1 winner; leading stable is 11% with AW 2yos (five seasons) but 1-3 with them this term; market check suggested.

runners_data.name: Mohaymenah
runners_data.spotlight: By Minzaal; first foal; dam 6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 93); 11-1 at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago when racing prominently before weakening; looked likely to be suited by this slightly longer trip; needs to take a good step up on that effort to be involved.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.comment: 20,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-sister to six winners; one of two newcomers for the yard
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to six winners, the best being In The Breeze (1m2f/1m4f; RPR 91); backed at double-figure odds on debut, when green but keeping on well to be under 3l third at Yarmouth (5f, good) last week; promising start; step up in trip should suit; contender.

runners_data.name: Angel Sense
runners_data.comment: Promising second on Kempton debut last week and she should improve for the experience
runners_data.spotlight: Showed signs of greenness when a close second at Kempton (6f, Polytack) and when beaten a similar distance in third at Nottingham (6f, good; favourite) where she improved; not ruled out.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Comprador
runners_data.note: Prominent racer switching to 7f for first time, could benefit from the extra furlong but needs to prove stamina
runners_data.comment: Third in his three qualifying runs; makes handicap debut for a yard in flying form
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent without progressing in four AW runs (6f) for Ed Walker this year; changed hands for 16,000gns last month; improvement for today's extra furlong is essential.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in excellent form with a recent 7f win, perfectly suited to strong pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Had issues with the stalls as a 2yo but she has returned from a winter break as an improved performer, winning a 7f handicap at Kempton this month and failing narrowly over C&D 11 days ago; should still have more to offer; one of two live chances for Ollie Sangster.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 258-day break, unclear how sharp she'll be after such a long absence
runners_data.spotlight: She didn't quite live up to market expectation in three turf runs as a 2yo but there were clear signs of encouragement with her three in-frame efforts; not obviously thrown in for this handicap/seasonal debut but the trainer is in form and Oisin Murphy is always a significant booking for the stable (57 wins and a further 63 second/third place finishes from 217 rides; level-stake profit of +37); market confidence would heighten interest.

runners_data.name: Night Mission
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping in class with form figures reading better than recent performances suggest
runners_data.spotlight: Second or third in his three runs in 2yo novice events (all 6f, good ground or slower); unplaced in two 6f handicaps this year but he drops in class today and his pedigree strongly suggests stepping up to 7f will help; finished behind Dublin Bay at Ascot last time but was racing away from the main action; well drawn and a return to more positive tactics could see him run a big race.

runners_data.name: Paranjape
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with course form, best recent effort was over 6f so stamina for 7f remains unproven
runners_data.spotlight: 6f maiden win here last November; stayed on for second of 12 in a Southwell handicap last month (6f); that race is yet to throw up a subsequent winner (as of before racing on Thursday) and he himself has since failed to fire at Haydock; stamina not assured.

runners_data.name: Dublin Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who will ensure strong gallop but may pay for early exertions in testing ground
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for the switch to nurseries last summer, winning easily at Ffos Las and Doncaster (both 6f) before finishing off strongly for sixth in a much stronger race at York's Ebor meeting; better than ever when winning a C&D handicap in April and his subsequent fifth of 19 at Ascot was in a Class 4; could still rate higher; key player despite a wider draw than ideal.

runners_data.name: Horwich
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has dropped 10lb in weights and won twice course and distance when sharp
runners_data.comment: Won twice over C&D for Clive Cox; has run moderately in handicaps for new yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first two starts, both over C&D, when trained by Clive Cox; struggled initially in handicaps for Ruth Carr but having dropped 10lb in the weights there were more encouraging signs over C&D 11 days ago (nearly 2l behind Court Of Stars), travelling strongly but just tapped for speed early in the straight; another 2lb lower here and he now has something to build on.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form has collapsed on turf but retains ability on all-weather surfaces
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark in a 6f maiden here on his reappearance in March; fair third at Southwell later that month but his form has nosedived on turf (handled it fine as a 2yo) on his last two starts (both in cheekpieces which are absent today); hopes pinned on the step up to 7f and the return to AW sparking a revival.

runners_data.name: Inferno
runners_data.note: Front-runner adding tongue-tie and blinkers but showed no improvement when stepped up in trip recently
runners_data.spotlight: No improvement for the switch to handicaps at Nottingham three weeks ago (8.3f, good), unable to land a blow; a tongue-tie and blinkers are now added but he is drawn wide and hasn't looked to be crying out for the drop to 7f.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ended last season well but has struggled in two handicap attempts this year
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in both starts since returning last month; needs a resurgence
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a pair of wins in Kempton nurseries (1m and 7f); he has struggled in two handicaps this time around, however, and comes here with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 121-day break with tongue-tie retained, fitness could be a concern
runners_data.spotlight: She was not beaten far in a pair of Kempton fillies' maidens (1m and 7f) in January, improving for the addition of a tongue-tie; neither race appeals as strong form though and she looks up against it now handicapping from the widest stall.

races.paceDynamic: Dublin Bay, Flyta, and Inferno will ensure a strong gallop from the gates, with Dublin Bay and Flyta both confirmed front-runners who rarely settle off the pace. This trio will string the field out early and maintain a searching gallop throughout the 7f trip on Wolverhampton's testing all-weather surface. The relentless pace will expose stamina limitations and create perfect conditions for hold-up horses to pick off tired leaders. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers and prominent racers with proven staying power who can finish through beaten horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Dublin Bay and Flyta engage early and maintain a searching gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The pace will string out the field and expose stamina deficiencies, allowing patient hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. Court Of Stars and Horwich benefit most from their proven ability to finish strongly when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners neutralise each other or go too fast too soon
scenarios.body: One of the leaders will steal a march when the pace slackens, with prominent racers ideally placed to capitalise. Comprador and Enamorus are best positioned to exploit a tactical affair from their forward positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Dublin Bay dominates the pace and maintains an even gallop without weakening
scenarios.body: The consistent tempo will favour horses with proven stamina at the trip who can sustain their effort. Chapman's Peak and Court Of Stars have the best combination of pace and staying power for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start with multiple horses vying for the lead
scenarios.body: The race will become a sprint from the 2f marker, suiting horses with natural pace over stamina. Paranjape and Wyle Cop have the best turn of foot for a tactical finish.

watchPoints.text: Dublin Bay and Flyta will dictate the pace but both face fitness concerns after breaks of 21 and 121 days respectively
Court Of Stars must overcome her hold-up style against a strong pace, but Billy Loughnane excels at getting horses home late
Enamorus represents Hugo Palmer returning from a winter break but 258 days off is excessive even with her class edge
Horwich has the ideal low weight of 124lbs and proven course form, making him a live outsider if the pace suits
Chapman's Peak needs to recapture his late-2024 form but Ed Dunlop's 3-from-18 record suggests patience required

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: True Promise
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong 5f-6f Tapeta form but faces traffic issues with four others wanting similar positions
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins on Tapeta elsewhere, at 5f-7f, all in 2024; has been involved in several tight finishes since December, including for Oisin Murphy at Kempton (6f) in April, and while he's been on much the same mark throughout, he's worth another go over a bare 5f; thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent C&D record including two wins here, benefits from likely strong pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Has a good C&D record which includes two wins in February, and there wasn't much she could do about her latest defeat on this track, when third to one well ahead of his mark; down in grade and one to consider in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Hedge Fund
runners_data.note: Lone front runner can dictate fractions but winless since 2yo season and needs to prove stamina at this trip
runners_data.comment: Everything went wrong on his comeback and he's entitled to improve for that down 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 6f on this track as 2yo; winless since that season but he's shown enough to think he can be placed to advantage off a reduced mark; had a troubled start to the season at Beverley but it's too soon to write him off; hood refitted with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Dark Kestrel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse often slowly away but C&D winner with three AW victories this year, suits patient ride
runners_data.comment: Beaten returned to turf last time; still three years since sole win in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner whose five AW wins include two this year; often slowly away; has been running respectably off his lower turf mark of late but probably needs a bit more for the adding of a visor.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form has declined this term, needs to prove AW effectiveness having struggled at Newcastle
runners_data.comment: Second here in 2025; 6lb below his last winning mark; has plenty in his favour
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 5f turf form in 2025 but his season slowed down later in the year and he's been below best, despite the reduced mark, this term; 0-3 on Newcastle AW but he did handle that Tapeta earlier in his career, so perhaps the switch to this track might pay off in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Spendmore Lane
runners_data.note: Can lead but often slowly away, recent 5f winner who absorbed weight rises but may get caught in traffic
runners_data.spotlight: Often leads but can be slowly away; took a steep rise in the weights for two 5f wins in early spring but she absorbed it and added another win, from the fast-finishing Ancient State, on Lingfield AW in April; another solid effort back on turf there 11 days ago; strong showing likely back at 5f on AW.

runners_data.name: Blue Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 46-day break, has C&D win but form declined since December
runners_data.comment: Finished race off well for 3rd at Wolverhampton nine days ago; 1lb lower today; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Has won on all three Tapeta tracks, most recently over C&D in December, not as good since and although he ran better back here in April, he found little at Newcastle next time; others more likely.

runners_data.name: Mick's Spirit
runners_data.note: Consistent 8yo prominent runner with excellent Polytrack record but finished behind key rivals recently
runners_data.spotlight: Cracking 8yo who has won two Polytrack races in every season for the last five years; however, he finished behind Spendmore Lane and Ancient State at Lingfield recently and the return to Tapeta looks a negative.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with four C&D wins but latest was in 2024, better recent turf form suggests AW struggles
runners_data.comment: Conditions no problem and he went close off this mark at Beverley ten days ago; well drawn
runners_data.spotlight: Four C&D wins but the latest was back in 2024 and he's struggled a bit here off this sort of mark in recent attempts; has been running well on turf of late, though, and he shouldn't be that far away.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three recent 5f AW wins, looked ahead of handicap mark and suits patient tactics
runners_data.spotlight: Looked ahead of his mark in first three 5f wins on the AW, most recently at Southwell in March; missed a beat at the start and only just failed to reel in the more prominently ridden Spendmore Lane at Lingfield since; raised a further 3lb but still has potential.

races.paceDynamic: Hedge Fund will lead unopposed early as the only genuine front runner, with True Promise, Curious Rover, Blue Force, Mick's Spirit and Jojo Rabbit all wanting prominent positions creating a congested pack behind. This clustering of five prominent runners will create traffic problems and scrimmaging from 2f out as they fight for racing room. The uncontested early leader Hedge Fund can dictate a steady pace before the prominent brigade engage, while hold-up horses Alondra, Dark Kestrel, Spendmore Lane and Ancient State get clean runs from the back. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the traffic carnage and finish fastest when others have used their energy battling for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hedge Fund sets modest fractions and the prominent pack gets congested.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes unsustainable as five horses jostle for position from 3f out, allowing the patient closers clean passage to sweep past tired leaders. Hold-up specialists with strong finishing kicks benefit from the set-up pace and positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early leader holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Hedge Fund gets soft fractions and the prominent brigade stalls each other.
scenarios.body: Tom Marquand can dictate perfect splits on Hedge Fund while the prominent runners neutralise each other's challenges through interference and position fighting. The uncontested leader kicks clear as others sort themselves out too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent pace battle
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quintet engage early and sustain strong gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: The five prominent runners create genuine pace pressure from 4f out, setting up the race for whoever can best handle the sustained tempo. This becomes a test of class and stamina rather than tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete traffic chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack bunches badly and causes significant interference.
scenarios.body: The congestion becomes so severe that several runners lose all chance, creating a lottery where positioning luck trumps ability. Horses drawn away from trouble or those getting clear runs benefit from others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Hedge Fund could steal this if allowed uncontested lead and slow fractions by the prominent pack
Traffic problems will develop from 3f out as True Promise, Curious Rover, Blue Force, Mick's Spirit and Jojo Rabbit converge
Alondra and Ancient State need clean runs from the back to utilise their finishing speed effectively
Spendmore Lane's gate speed crucial as slow start would force hold-up role against natural style
Blue Force returning from 46-day absence may need this run to reach peak fitness

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who should get ideal tracking position behind High Storm's likely lead
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly landed a 1m1f maiden at Yarmouth last September and he ran to a similar level when second at Bath on his reappearance last month (1m2f, good); gelded prior to his handicap debut at York (1m4f) two weeks ago, a race in which he was never far away but looked a bit awkward under pressure; upped 2lb but not yet exposed; AW debut.

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: Made all in his last win at Southwell and showed promise when taking the lead, could press High Storm early
runners_data.spotlight: Rounded off his 2yo campaign with a game 1m2f win at Pontefract (soft), after which he was gelded; made all to beat his sole opponent in a Southwell match (1m4f) last month but he could manage only third behind that reopposing rival at Chester (a solid effort nevertheless) three weeks ago; still capable of better; trainer also saddles High Storm.

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with tactical advantage in small field, though 44 days since last run raises fitness questions
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointed as favourite in a 1m2f handicap at Newmarket last month but his earlier Doncaster win (1m2f, good to soft) was encouraging; promise on AW in February; should stay 1m4f and he is not fully exposed just yet; Karl Burke is also responsible for Galilean Quality.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Needs strong pace to be effective but Murphy's presence adds tactical value in slowly-run race
runners_data.spotlight: Made heavy weather of it when landing a 9.4f novice here in January (2-5 favourite); better in form terms when second of eight in a Chester handicap three weeks ago (extended 1m4f, good; Galilean Quality third) but he looked a tricky ride in the straight, hanging both ways; has the ability to deal with a 3lb rise but there are reservations.

races.paceDynamic: High Storm stands alone as the confirmed front-runner in this small field, likely to dictate terms from the gate without early pressure. Baltic Fleet, Galilean Quality, and Mythical Bay all show prominent tendencies but none are natural pace-pressers, suggesting they'll settle behind High Storm's lead. The moderate early tempo will allow High Storm to control fractions through the middle sections before the field closes late. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the leader, as the race will lack the early burn needed to set up hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Storm Controls
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: The front-runner dictates comfortable fractions and kicks clear in the straight before late challenges materialize. His February AW form and tactical advantage of controlling the race tempo makes him very dangerous.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners settles perfectly behind High Storm
scenarios.body: Baltic Fleet or Galilean Quality track the leader's moderate pace and produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out. The race becomes a straight fight between early positioned horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes very slow and the field bunches
scenarios.body: Mythical Bay gets the strong pace he needs for his finishing kick as the field compresses turning for home. Murphy's tactical skills help him find racing room when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm stops quickly after leading too easily
scenarios.body: The front-runner's effort flattens dramatically in the final furlong after dictating overly slow fractions. One of the prominent runners capitalizes on his sudden vulnerability.

watchPoints.text: High Storm could prove unbeatable if allowed to dictate easy fractions from the front in this small field
Baltic Fleet's gelding operation and 15-day break since Bath second could produce significant improvement
Galilean Quality might challenge High Storm for the early lead given his front-running tendencies at Southwell
Mythical Bay needs the pace to collapse late to have any realistic chance from his likely rearward position
